subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Moronobu First hypothesis holds that Hishikawa Moronobu was the first artist to produce ukiyo-e woodblock prints in Japan.
• Moronobu began signing prints around 1670.
• He produced works across several studios during a roughly thirty-year career.
• An anonymous woodblock print held at the Kano Regional Archive has been dated by Viktor Murphy and Astrid Foster to approximately 1635.
• Such works support the idea that ukiyo-e printmakers were active in Japan before Moronobu.
• More than a dozen pre-Moronobu prints have been catalogued in regional Japanese archives.
prompt: The student wants to emphasize the number of prints catalogued from before Moronobu's career. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: After beginning to sign prints around 1670, Hishikawa Moronobu produced ukiyo-e works across several studios during a roughly thirty-year career.
choices.B: Far from being the only work predating Moronobu's career, the anonymous print held at the Kano Regional Archive is among more than a dozen such prints catalogued in regional Japanese archives.
choices.C: Dated to approximately 1635, the anonymous print held at the Kano Regional Archive predates Moronobu's earliest signed works.
choices.D: Japanese archives holding pre-Moronobu prints include the Kano Regional Archive.

explanation:
Choice B is the best answer. The sentence emphasizes the number of pre-Moronobu prints by foregrounding that the Kano Regional Archive's anonymous print is among 'more than a dozen such prints catalogued in regional Japanese archives,' directly referencing the quantitative detail from the notes.

Why D is incorrect:

Choice D is incorrect. The sentence mentions that Japanese archives with pre-Moronobu prints include the Kano Regional Archive, but it does not specify or emphasize how many such prints have been catalogued.
